papers.title: Evaluation of the Stress-Shielding Effect of a PEEK Knee Prosthesis. A Finite Element Study
papers.abstract: Background: The long-term success of total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is often compromised by stress shielding, which can lead to bone resorption and even implant loosening. This study employs finite element analysis (FEA) to compare the stress-shielding effects of a knee prosthesis made from polyether ether ketone (PEEK) with a traditional titanium Ti6Al4V implant on an osteoporotic tibial bone model. Methods: Stress distribution and the stress-shielding factor (SSF) were evaluated at seven critical points in the proximal tibia under physiological loading conditions. Results: Results indicate that the PEEK prosthesis yields a more uniform stress transmission, with von Mises stress levels within the optimal 2–3 MPa range for bone maintenance and consistently negative or near-zero SSF values, implying minimal stress shielding. Conversely, titanium implants exhibited significant stress shielding with high positive SSF values across all points. Additionally, stress concentrations on the polyethylene liner were lower and more evenly distributed in the PEEK model, suggesting reduced wear potential. Conclusions: These findings highlight the biomechanical advantages of PEEK in reducing stress shielding and preserving bone integrity, supporting its potential use to improve implant longevity in TKA. Further experimental and clinical validation are warranted.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是PEEK膝关节假体与钛合金钛6铝4V的应力遮挡比较，并非针对钛6铝4V股骨柄的增材制造设计，因此与方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on a knee prosthesis, not a femoral hip stem; it does not address additive manufacturing, stem structural design, lattice architectures, or fatigue testing for Ti-6Al-4V femoral stems.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较PEEK和钛合金膝关节假体的应力遮挡效应
summary_zh.method: 有限元分析评估胫骨近端应力分布和应力遮挡因子
summary_zh.result: PEEK假体应力分布更均匀，应力遮挡更小
summary_zh.validation: 仅有限元模拟，无实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To compare stress-shielding effects of PEEK versus titanium alloy Ti6Al4V knee prostheses.
summary_en.method: Finite element analysis evaluated von Mises stress and stress-shielding factor at seven critical points on an osteoporotic tibial bone model under physiological loads.
summary_en.result: The PEEK prosthesis exhibited more uniform stress transmission with values within the optimal range and minimal stress shielding, unlike the titanium implant.
summary_en.validation: Finite element simulation without experimental validation.

papers.title: Novel high cycle vibration-based fatigue test for pure shear loading
papers.abstract: Aeronautical components are frequently subjected to multiaxial stresses. Producing representative fatigue data is compromised by the high costs and extended durations of traditional tests. This work proposes a novel high cycle vibration-based fatigue method for pure shear. A design protocol was followed to develop a specimen capable of inducing this specific stress state during resonance conditions. The stress state was validated experimentally using a strain rosette. The proposed methodology was subsequently applied to characterize the fatigue behavior of Ti-6Al-4V fabricated via L-PBF with as-built surfaces. The fatigue strengths obtained at around 700 Hz proved to be in accordance with available results from standard torsion tests at 5 Hz. All fatigue initiations occurred within the high stress zone and far from the edges. Fractography analysis revealed that all failures were linked to typical additive manufacturing discontinuities, such as lack of fusion and surface roughness features. The use of flat plate specimens proved advantageous for analyzing the influence of surface characteristics on fatigue behavior, as they offer superior visibility of crack initiation and propagation compared to cylindrical geometries. Furthermore, the significant reduction in test duration underscores the efficiency of the proposed approach for investigating the effects of cyclic shear stress. • Innovative pure shear fatigue tests at 700 Hz using an electrodynamic shaker. • Torsion testes using plate specimens easing surface investigation. • Multiaxial fatigue data acquired 140× faster than conventional torsion tests. • Characterization of pure shear fatigue resistance of Ti–6Al–4V L-BPF with as-built surfaces.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文提出了一种新型高频振动疲劳测试方法，用于评估激光粉末床熔融Ti-6Al-4V合金在纯剪切载荷下的疲劳性能，与标准扭转试验结果一致。
llm.why_not_core: This paper concentrates solely on pure shear fatigue and does not cover tensile/compressive or multiaxial fatigue behavior that is also common in structural applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统疲劳测试成本高、周期长，需开发高效方法。
summary_zh.method: 设计了共振纯剪切试样，在700Hz下进行振动疲劳试验，并用应变花验证应力状态。
summary_zh.result: 获得的疲劳强度与标准扭转试验一致，裂纹起裂于典型增材制造缺陷处。
summary_zh.validation: 通过应变花测量和断口分析验证了纯剪切状态及失效机制。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the high cost and long duration of conventional fatigue tests for multiaxial stresses.
summary_en.method: A resonance-based fatigue specimen was designed to achieve pure shear loading, validated by a strain rosette, and tested at 700 Hz using an electrodynamic shaker.
summary_en.result: The fatigue strengths of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V with as-built surfaces matched standard torsion tests at 5 Hz, with all failures initiating at process-related discontinuities.
summary_en.validation: Stress state validation via strain measurement and fractography confirmed pure shear conditions and failure mechanisms.

papers.title: Establishing Rational Processing Parameters for Dry Finish-Milling of SLM Ti6Al4V over Metal Removal Rate and Tool Wear
papers.abstract: The study is motivated by the application of dry finish milling for post-build processing of additive Ti6Al4V blanks, since the use of neither lubricant nor coolants has been attracting increasing attention due to its environmental benefits, non-toxicity, and the elimination of the need for additional cleaning processes. For end mills, wear patterns were investigated upon finish milling of the SLM Ti6Al4V samples under various machining conditions (by varying the values of radial depth of cut and feed values at a constant level of axial depth of cut and cutting speed). When using all the applied milling modes, the identical tool wear mechanism was revealed. Built-up edges mainly developed on the leading surfaces, increasing the surface roughness on the SLM Ti6Al4V samples but protecting the cutting edges. However, abrasive wear was mainly characteristic of the flank surfaces that accelerated peeling of the protective coatings and increased wear of the end mills. The following milling parameters have been established as being close to rational ones: Vc = 60 m/min, Vf = 400 mm/min, ap = 4 mm, and ae = 0.4 mm. They affected the surface roughness of the SLM Ti6Al4V samples in the following way: max cutting thickness—8 μm; built-up edge at rake surface—50 ± 3 μm; max wear of flank surface—15 ± 1 μm; maximum adherence of workpiece. Mode III provided the maximum MRR value and negligible wear of the end mill, but its main disadvantage was the high average surface roughness on the SLM Ti6Al4V sample. Mode II was characterized by both the lowest average surface roughness and the lowest wear of the end mill, as well as an insufficient MRR value. Since these two modes differed only in their feed rates, their values should be optimized in the range from 200 to 400 mm/min.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了SLM Ti6Al4V的干式精铣后处理工艺参数，但未涉及疲劳或力学性能，仅关注表面粗糙度和刀具磨损。
llm.why_not_core: The paper investigates machining parameters for dry finish-milling of SLM Ti6Al4V but does not evaluate mechanical performance (fatigue, tensile) or microstructure effects relevant to post-processing control.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究干式精铣对SLM Ti6Al4V后处理的适用性，追求环保和成本效益。
summary_zh.method: 改变径向切深和进给量，分析刀具磨损机制和表面粗糙度。
summary_zh.result: 确定了优化铣削参数，主要磨损机制为积屑瘤和磨粒磨损。
summary_zh.validation: 通过多模式实验测量表面粗糙度和刀具磨损验证。

summary_en.motivation: To establish rational dry finish-milling parameters for post-processing of SLM Ti6Al4V, focusing on environmental benefits and cost reduction.
summary_en.method: Varying radial depth of cut and feed rate at constant axial depth and cutting speed to analyze tool wear patterns and surface roughness.
summary_en.result: Identified near-optimal milling parameters and characterized built-up edge and abrasive wear mechanisms.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurement of surface roughness and tool wear across multiple machining modes.
